entry.note: Kuhlmann-Matusinski surreal exp-log equivalence. Fits Surreal Numbers appendix. Cited in calculus-up-to-epsilon.ts (cites array).

relevance.rationale: Identity confirmed from the document's own cover (arXiv:1203.4538v1 [math.AC], exponential-logarithmic equivalence classes of surreal numbers, two authors) and matches the seeded key. Single citation site: folio/quantum-observable-universe/appendix-surreals/calculus-up-to-epsilon.ts:19, inside the `cites:` array. NOT load-bearing: the sibling calculus-up-to-epsilon.md never mentions exponential or logarithmic equivalence classes anywhere. Its five numbered sections are the Jackson q-derivative as native d/dx, the Berarducci-Mantova derivation and its right inverse, limits-as-evaluations at omega, formal power series, and the Loeb hyperfinite measure — the surreal results it actually consumes are Gonshor's exp/log and Berarducci-Mantova's derivation, both of which the prose names explicitly and neither of which is this document. The document's own main result (a recursive and sign-sequence description of the representatives of minimal length of the exponential equivalence classes) has no consumer in the block. Verdict supporting rather than tangential: it is genuinely part of the surreal exp/log literature the appendix sits in, and per the AGENTS.md surreal-narrowing ledger this whole area is Language-tier, so a background cite is appropriate — it is simply not doing work.

proposedActions.rationale: A background entry in a cites-array for an appendix in the same subject area is a legitimate, low-cost citation. Flagging it as 'must be surfaced inline' would inflate its role; the honest record is that no corpus claim depends on it.
